questions.q: What is the base spirit of a Caipirinha, muddled in the glass with lime and sugar?
questions.exp: Cachaça, Brazil's spirit distilled from fresh sugarcane juice, is the base. The Codex builds the drink with half a lime cut in wedges and two teaspoons of sugar muddled in a rocks glass, then the cachaça and crushed ice, and the lime wedges are the garnish.

questions.q: A sugar cube soaked in Angostura bitters sits in the flute of a Champagne Cocktail. Which spirit goes in before the wine?
questions.exp: The Codex's Champagne Cocktail drops the bitters soaked cube into a flute, adds 15 ml of Cognac and tops it slowly with Champagne, with a lemon twist. Older recipes leave the brandy out, so the house spec decides at the bar.

questions.q: Which juice gives a Cosmopolitan its pink colour, shaken with citrus vodka, Cointreau and lime?
questions.exp: Cranberry juice colours the Cosmopolitan: 40 ml citrus vodka, 15 ml Cointreau, 15 ml lime juice and 30 ml cranberry, shaken and strained up into a cocktail glass. The garnish is an orange twist, often flamed, or a lime wheel.

questions.q: Which spirit is shaken with lemon and sugar syrup, then topped with Champagne, in the Codex's French 75?
questions.exp: The French 75 is 30 ml gin, 15 ml lemon juice and 10 ml sugar syrup shaken, strained into a flute and topped with Champagne, finished with a lemon twist. New Orleans bars often build it on Cognac instead, so ask which the guest expects.

questions.q: What garnish turns a Dry Martini into a Gibson?
questions.exp: A Gibson is a Dry Martini, gin with a little dry vermouth stirred and strained up, garnished with a cocktail onion in place of the lemon twist or the olive. The base and the mixer stay the same; only the garnish changes the name.

questions.q: Which liqueur goes into the flute first for a Kir Royale, before about 100 ml of Champagne is poured over it?
questions.exp: A Kir Royale is 10 to 15 ml of crème de cassis, the blackcurrant liqueur of Burgundy, topped slowly with Champagne and served without a garnish. Made with Bourgogne Aligoté in place of the Champagne, it is a plain Kir.

questions.q: Besides aged Jamaican rum, Martinique rhum, orange curaçao and lime, which syrup goes into the 1944 Mai Tai?
questions.exp: Orgeat, an almond syrup scented with orange flower water, sweetens the original Mai Tai of 1944, shaken with crushed ice and poured unstrained into a rocks glass. A mint sprig and the spent lime shell are the garnish; the pineapple versions came later.

questions.q: What tops the vodka and lime of a Moscow Mule, built over ice in a copper mug?
questions.exp: The Moscow Mule is 45 ml vodka and 15 ml lime juice topped with ginger beer, built over ice in a copper mug or a highball. A lime wedge and a mint sprig are the garnish; ginger ale is sweeter and milder and makes a different drink.

questions.q: Which French aromatised wine joins gin and vodka in a Vesper?
questions.exp: The Codex's Vesper is 60 ml gin, 20 ml vodka and 10 ml Lillet Blanc, served up in a chilled coupe with a wide lemon twist. The novel asked for it shaken; most houses stir it.

questions.q: Which herbal liqueur goes by the bar spoon into a Vieux Carré of rye, Cognac and sweet vermouth?
questions.exp: The Vieux Carré takes equal parts rye, Cognac and sweet vermouth, a bar spoon of Bénédictine and a dash each of Angostura and Peychaud's, garnished with a lemon twist or a cherry. It was born in the French Quarter of New Orleans in the 1930s.

questions.q: What garnish does the Codex give a classic Manhattan of rye, sweet vermouth and Angostura?
questions.exp: A brandied cherry finishes the Manhattan: 60 ml rye, 30 ml sweet vermouth and two dashes of Angostura, stirred and strained up into a coupe. A Dry Manhattan, made with dry vermouth alone, takes a lemon twist instead.

questions.q: Besides a lime wheel, what goes on the rim of a Margarita glass, on one side only so the guest can choose?
questions.exp: The Margarita's garnish is a lime wheel and a half salt rim, so the guest can drink with or without it. The base is blanco tequila of 100 per cent agave, with lime juice and Cointreau or triple sec, shaken and served up or over ice.
